newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Wednesday on continued long liquidation from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,160 yuan ($381), losing 14 yuan. It opened at 3,170 yuan and hit a high of 3,174 yuan per tonne.
November fell six to 3,140 yuan, the January 1998 contract 95 3,045 and March 12 to 3,120 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 21,600 tonnes from 19,900 tonnes.
Soybeans opened lower and fell further before all contracts closed at their intraday lows, traders said.
"Many retail investors liquidated their long positions today as they see little chance for the market to recover after long-term weak sentiment," one trader said.
"Technical charts also indicated downward potential in the next few days," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall further in the short term.
